observable_outcome: A cursor the Backlog route just returned is accepted by the very next request against real persistence, so the Backlog can be paged past its first page at all. Measured at a258ed2 against the local Firestore emulator, it cannot be: GET /v1/requirements returns next_cursor, the next request carrying that cursor fails, and the cause is that internal/store/firestore's paged reads hand StartAfter a value they built as collectionPath + slash + key while ordering by firestore.DocumentID -- and the Go client, whose own contract is that a string cursor for a DocumentID order is the document id RELATIVE to the queried collection, prefixes the collection's full resource name a second time. The server then rejects a parent name in which the installation and collection segments appear twice, and internal/api reports that storage-side InvalidArgument to the caller as 400 invalid_request, which is why a server defect read as a bad cursor for three exercises. The fix is entirely inside the one layer allowed to know about document ids: one named helper returning the collection-relative document id, called by both defective paged reads. Nothing the route returns changes -- measured, the cursor already carries only the domain Requirement id in an opaque v1 envelope and leaks no client representation -- no page bound is widened, no index is added, and the in-memory adapter, which is self-consistent rather than accidentally passing, changes not at all. What fixes the outcome is one test name present in BOTH adapter packages that walks the cursor to exhaustion and asserts the pages concatenate to every record exactly once with no duplicate and no omission, plus an executable HTTP walk over the real control-plane binary and the real emulator, plus a test that every cursor shape refused today is still refused with 400.
acceptance_criteria: A1. Scope boundary, written into the evidence before any code is edited, as a table with one row each. (1) What this task makes true: a cursor the Backlog route returned is accepted by the next request against real persistence, and the concatenation of pages covers every record exactly once, on BOTH adapters. (2) What it deliberately does not do: it changes no byte of what the route returns, it widens no page bound, it adds no Firestore index, it changes no document id and no stored field, it changes no query shape, filter or ordering, and it changes the in-memory adapter's behaviour not at all. (3) What it records but does not fix: that internal/api's domainError defaults to 400 invalid_request for any unclassified error, which dressed a storage-side InvalidArgument as a caller mistake (dp-v2-079 d7); that the two adapters do not share one total order because base64url is not order-preserving (d4); and that internal/application/allocation.go and release_surface.go consume the first page of an adapter-specific order (d4). (4) What only a later task can establish: the cap-backlog-visibility verdict, which needs the M5 re-dogfood (d10). (5) That this task passes no release gate on its own.

A2. Baseline, measured before changing anything. A3. Reproduce the defect yourself before fixing it, and record the argv and the verdict of each reproduction. (a) At the ROUTE layer over real persistence: with the Firestore emulator running, drive Service.ListRequirementsPage (or the HTTP route) with page_size=1 and feed the returned next_cursor into the next call; record the error verbatim. Expected at a258ed2: a gRPC InvalidArgument whose parent name repeats the installations/<key>/<collection> pair twice and which reports a missing slash at a byte index. (b) At the EventsPage layer: the identical failure, reproduced and not inferred. (c) Record that the same command WITHOUT the emulator is green because the cases skip, and state in those words that such a run measures nothing and is never a pass (gate rule G7).

A4. Settle the client contract by measurement, in a check of its own, and record all six variants with their verdicts. Against the emulator, on a collection ordered by firestore.DocumentID, call StartAfter with each of: the collection path joined to the document id; the bare document id; the last row's *DocumentRef; the last row's *DocumentSnapshot; a fabricated document id that no document has; and a *DocumentRef built from a DIFFERENT collection of the same installation. Record which returned an error and which returned rows, with the row counts. The measurement that decides the design is that the bare document id, the ref and the snapshot all return the identical page, that the joined path is refused, and that the ref from another collection is SILENTLY ACCEPTED and returns the whole unfiltered page -- the client's own source carries an unimplemented TODO at exactly that branch. If any of these verdicts disagrees with dp-v2-079 d1 or d2, stop and escalate rather than proceeding on the design's assumption.

A5. The fix. Add one unexported helper in internal/store/firestore/store.go -- documentIDCursor(afterID string) (string, error) -- returning PathKey(afterID), with a doc comment that states the client contract verbatim (a string cursor under a DocumentID order is the document id RELATIVE to the queried collection, and the client prefixes the collection's own full resource name itself) and names the InvalidArgument it replaces. Call it from RequirementsPage (store.go:633 at a258ed2) and from EventsPage (:763), replacing both open-coded path-joining expressions. Do NOT pass a *DocumentRef or a *DocumentSnapshot: A4 measures why the ref form is the weaker guard. Leave ExpiredActiveLeases (:957) untouched -- it already passes a bare last.Ref.ID and is already covered by internal/store/firestore/store_test.go:316-326.

A6. The outcome test, ONE name in BOTH adapter packages: TestThePageCursorTheCallerWasHandedIsAcceptedByTheNextPageUntilEveryRequirementIsCoveredOnce, in internal/store/firestore/store_test.go and in internal/store/memory/store_test.go. Each seeds N Requirements with N strictly greater than 3, drives Service.ListRequirementsPage (so the opaque-cursor envelope is exercised, not just the port) with page_size 1, and feeds every returned next_cursor into the next call until a page returns none. Assert: every page except possibly the last has exactly page_size rows; the terminal page carries no cursor; the walk terminates within a bound derived from N and never by a timer; and the concatenation of pages equals the seeded id set as a MULTISET -- no duplicate, no omission. Then repeat the entire walk at a second page size that does NOT divide N and assert the same set. Assert NOTHING about the order ids arrive in, and say why in the test's own comment: base64url is not order-preserving, so the two adapters order differently and an order assertion would pass on memory and fail on Firestore for a reason unrelated to the cursor (dp-v2-079 d4).

A7. The EventsPage counterpart, same two packages, same single name: TestTheEventPageCursorTheCallerWasHandedIsAcceptedByTheNextPageUntilEveryEventIsCoveredOnce. Same walk-to-exhaustion, same multiset coverage assertion, same absence of any order assertion, driven through the EventsPage port because no route exposes it.
